cases.why: Measured false positive: three of the first seven buyer signals against real posts were a contractor, a freelancer and a founder asking how to find customers. They sell their own time; they are peers, not buyers.

record.title: I run a solo dev agency and want more work
record.text: I am an experienced developer and I freelance for US clients. My contract ended and I am trying to find clients for automation projects. How do I get clients in this space?

cases.why: Measured false positive, and the worst one: a well-written essay on organisational speed, cross-posted to two communities and scored as a buyer twice.

record.title: Implementation is instant now and the org around it moves at the same speed as always
record.text: We all know large organisations are slow. In my experience the manual work gets automated and the meetings stay exactly where they were. Generally speaking nothing changes.

cases.why: Hard reject: however much pain a hiring post describes, it is a job advert. Pain plus a budget still is not a buyer when they are buying an employee.

record.title: We run a small agency and everything is still done by hand
record.text: Invoicing, scheduling and reporting are all manual and it costs us days every month. We are hiring an operations engineer to fix it.
